clue.text: Nuts for a bird

definitions.meaning: nuts in the slang sense of crazy, mad
a grey bird famous for its two-note call and for laying eggs in other nests

explanation.surface: Someone asks which bird nuts are meant to feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: slang for crazy, and the name of a well-known parasitic bird.

clue.text: Muslim symbol in street

definitions.meaning: the curved moon shape associated with Islam
a curved street of houses, common in British place names

explanation.definitionFit: The curved moon emblem of Islam shares its name with a curved row of houses.

clue.text: Class actors close to stage

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word stage, its final letter

explanation.surface: A group of performers come near the theatre platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'near', but means the end of 'stage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in India.

clue.text: Work in one, on view

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A piece of art seen as a whole, now on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a belief or judgement someone holds, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A duke keeping goddess entertained

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the goddess sits inside the first pieces

parts.note: a Muse is one of the nine Greek goddesses of the arts

explanation.surface: A nobleman entertains a goddess at his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entertained by something is being diverted or made to smile by it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dramatist has extra holding whopper

indicators.note: holding means the word for extra keeps the whopper inside it

parts.note: more means additional or extra
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A playwright hires an extra actor who is enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whopper' suggests something big, but here it is a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French comic playwright.

clue.text: Son, mischievous child, revealed dope

parts.note: an imp is a naughty child
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: A naughty boy gives away where the drugs are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs, but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, the same as a fool or dimwit.

clue.text: In Aden, I always find abstinence

indicators.note: In says the answer lies within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A traveller in the Yemeni port always goes without.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-denial, refusing oneself pleasures, is a form of abstinence.

clue.text: Either originally inside going hungry, or eating heartily

indicators.note: inside tells us the opening letter goes within the word for going hungry

parts.note: going without food is fasting

indicators.note: originally points to the very first letter of the word Either

explanation.surface: A choice between starving and gorging yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets two opposites side by side; 'going hungry' is wordplay and 'eating heartily' the definition, with 'or' just joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a large meal, so tucking into one with gusto is a fair synonym for gorging.

clue.text: Muck-rakers, say, amongst good crowd

indicators.note: amongst places the word for say among the letters of good and crowd

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Scandal-mongers are speaking up within a respectable throng.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESS as a crowd survives in 'the press of people'.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck-rakers are sensational journalists who dig up scandal, the trade of tabloid papers.

clue.text: Celebrity left, turning back on small French city

indicators.note: turning back means the celebrity and the left are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A famous person departs, heading back to a small town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' reverses NAME plus L to give LEMAN, and S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Mans is a city in north-west France, known for its 24-hour motor race.

clue.text: Leader of march wearing superb top

indicators.note: wearing means one thing has the other around it, so the leading letter goes inside

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent or superb

indicators.note: Leader of picks out the first letter of the word march

explanation.surface: The person heading a parade has a splendid top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like a garment beside 'wearing', but it is the definition: a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of achievement is the top of something.

clue.text: Cleaner hit badly is no longer in danger

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are damaged and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A cleaner who was struck in a bad way has now recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the letters of CLEANER and HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of trouble or free of suspicion is an idiom for being safe again.

clue.text: Report of an alpine cat seen by followers, contained in New Testament

indicators.note: contained in means the cat and the followers sit inside the Bible abbreviation

parts.note: the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a mountain cat
men are a leader's followers or troops

explanation.surface: Word of a snow leopard sighted by its devotees, recorded in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a public statement or declaration, so the two are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Art seldom represented as a great work

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Fine art rarely gets portrayed as a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges the letters of ART SELDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting by a great European painter of before about 1800 is called by this name.

clue.text: Poet's rewritten sonnet about New York

definitions.note: read as poet is, so the definition is the poet

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the city abbreviation
rewritten means the letters of sonnet are set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: A poet's sonnet has been redrafted about New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Let down after daughter is given a job

parts.note: being appointed is being given a post

explanation.surface: A parent feels deflated once their daughter lands employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling let down is feeling dissatisfied because hopes were not met, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Scatter seed round parking area by Rolls-Royce for a bird

indicators.note: round means the sowing word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to sow is to scatter seed
P is the sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Throwing seed around a car park next to a luxury car to feed a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown seed-eating bird, an example of the class.

clue.text: Person's heading off? Yes, northwards, making long journey

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word is cut away

parts.note: a body is a person, so person's is body's

indicators.note: in a down clue northwards means read from bottom to top, so backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is leaving, agreeing to head north on a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: BODY'S loses its first letter to ODYS; 'northwards' reverses YES to SEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's hero Odysseus took ten years to get home, so his name became a word for an epic journey.

clue.text: Some closures, ultimately, in consequence

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that certain shutdowns will eventually follow from something.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in consequence' as the definition, but that is an adverb phrase; the noun 'consequence' fits, with 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or effect of an action is its consequence, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Group tackling soldier approaching cathedral city alone

indicators.note: tackling suggests the group takes hold of the soldier, enclosing him

parts.note: a set is a group of things
a para is a paratrooper
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A gang takes on a soldier walking alone towards a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on one's own or apart from others is the adverbial sense here.

clue.text: Bishop with group

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
and means together with

explanation.surface: A bishop accompanied by a party of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of people, especially musicians, so these are synonyms.

clue.text: Busy person starts to chamfer hard wood

parts.note: a busy bee is a hard-working person

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A carpenter begins bevelling the edge of some tough timber.
explanation.walkthrough: To chamfer is to bevel an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech is a hardwood timber from the tree of the same name.

clue.text: One courting a woman may give diamonds, perhaps, then gold

parts.note: diamonds is one example of a suit in a pack of cards
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A wooer might present diamonds and then gold to win her.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has jewellery as gifts; diamonds is really a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who woos a woman with a view to marriage is her suitor.

clue.text: Anxiety of South American writers, English as well

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US forces
pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: Nervousness felt by Latin American authors, and by an English one too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one idea, but splits into S and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is a state of nervous uncertainty while awaiting an outcome, so anxiety fits.

clue.text: Cast bemused

definitions.meaning: cast as a past participle: hurled or tossed
confused or disconcerted, as in being put off one's stride

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past participle of the verb for hurl, and also means confused or disconcerted.

clue.text: Publicity involving husband by name, a joiner

indicators.note: involving means the publicity wraps around the husband

parts.note: hype is exaggerated publicity

explanation.surface: Press coverage of a married man is linked with his name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a joiner' hints at a carpenter but means a punctuation mark that links words.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark links two words or word parts, so it literally joins them.
